item.content:encoded:
MINNESOTA — Aaron Judge’s health has the Yankees holding their breath once again.
The slugger left Wednesday’s 5-4, 13-inning loss to the Twins prematurely when Heliot Ramos pinch-hit for him with a runner on and one out in the top of the sixth inning. The Yankees were only down two runs at the time, and Judge, initially expected to rest on Wednesday, was fresh off an off day.
A short time later, the Yankees announced that Judge exited the game with tightness in his right lower leg. The news comes with the right fielder just seven games removed from a 99-day absence for a stress fracture in his first right rib.
“Hopefully, it’s something we were able to catch,” Aaron Boone said after the game.
Neither Boone nor Judge specified what part of the body the latter hurt. Judge, always unrevealing when it comes to his injuries, wouldn’t even say it was his leg, stating he simply had a “lower body” issue.
Judge did say that he first felt something while playing the field in the first inning on Wednesday, but he couldn’t pinpoint a particular play. Boone said he no knowledge of an injury prior to Wednesday, and that he wasn’t made aware of the problem until he noticed Judge hobbling in the outfield on a play he wasn’t involved in during the bottom of the fifth inning.
Judge also appeared to grimace when he took a check swing on the first pitch of his third-inning at-bat.
“I tried to kind of play it off and see how long we could go, because these games are important down the stretch,” Judge said. “But in talking it over, I thought it’d be the right move to come out so we don’t cost the team in the field or on the basepaths.
“I didn’t think it was smart to push it too much here.”
There is no update on Aaron Judge as of this moment
🎥: @YESNetwork pic.twitter.com/hifw6hg9W5
— FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) September 16, 2026
Judge is facing his latest injury scare with just 10 games left in the regular season. The Yankees have the day off on Thursday before beginning a three-game series at Arizona’s Chase Field, a turfed surface that wouldn’t be friendly to a lower body injury. The second-place Yanks, who have already secured a playoff berth, will then host a crucial four-game series against the division-leading Rays from Sept. 22-24.
With the off day on Thursday, the Yankees will see how Judge responds to treatment. He said “I don’t know” and “probably not” when asked if he’ll get testing, though Boone wasn’t sure about that.
“Hopefully it’s just one little thing,” Judge said, “and then we’re back out there soon.”
Judge likened his leg issue to the types of nagging injuries that pop up during spring training and at the start of the season when players are ramping up their bodies. He has been doing just that since returning from his rib injury on Sept. 8.
“We’re still trying to ramp up, so there’s going to be little things like this that come up,” Judge said. “I just thought it’d be best to — instead of pushing through it like I normally do, and it might become a little worse — get somebody who’s ready to go in there and just try and do what’s best for the team.”
It should be noted that Judge’s rib rehab and pre-activation build-up skipped some steps. He got his wish after repeatedly making it clear that he wanted to forego a minor league rehab assignment despite missing over three months. The superstar also only faced living pitching once, and that came against some minor leaguers.
Asked if Wednesday’s injury made him rethink the process, Judge told the Daily News, “People blow out their calves and blow out their quads in rehab assignments, so I don’t think taking a game in Double-A will change any of that.”
He added that he felt his build-up has been gradual, as he had felt asymptomatic for weeks before returning.
“That’s what we kind of did with playing the [seven] innings, playing the eight innings,” Judge said, referring to his planned early exits in his first two games back, the first of which he said he was “not happy” about the night of.
Judge also had off on Sept. 10.
Prior to Wednesday, Boone had said that he’s been “pleased” with the way Judge has been responding physically since returning to game action. Judge, who has said he wants to be playing every day, said much of the same over the weekend.
The captain, who went 0-for-2 with two strikeouts before departing on Wednesday, hasn’t had much success at the plate since coming off the injured list as he searches for his timing. He did crush a three-run homer in Monday’s victory over the Twins, but he entered that game 3-for-17 (.176) with zero extra-base hits in his first five games back.
Still, the Yankees have been thrilled to have Judge back in a lineup that struggled mightily without him. With Judge’s mere presence impacting the way those around him are attacked, the Bombers had one of the worst offenses in baseball while the back-to-back MVP was on the IL, ranking last in K% (26.1%); 29th in wRC+ (90) and average (.227); 28th in wOBA (.299); 27th in OPS (.681); and 24th in runs scored (341) from June 2 through Sept. 7.
“I’m not sure exactly what’s going on, but it’s never good when your best player on your team comes out of the lineup,” Carlos Rodón said after battling some velocity issues and tightness of his own on Wednesday. “So obviously, I’m hoping he’s gonna be okay. I’m not sure exactly what’s happening, but I’m sure he’ll be fine.”
While it’s too soon to know if Judge will miss extended time, the Yankees will have limited options for his roster spot if that’s the case. There’s fellow outfielder Jasson Domínguez, but he cannot be trusted to play defense in the critical games that are coming up.
Utilityman Max Schuemann is another choice at Triple-A who can also play the outfield.
Of course, the Yankees are hoping it doesn’t come to that.
“Obviously, he’s a key figure to what we do,” Boone said. “Hopefully, we get it treated and knock it out and [he can] be a factor at some point.”

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Shohei Ohtani, Carlos Correa and more: How star injuries could reshape the MLB playoffs
item.dc:creator: Steve Henson
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - - As October approaches, injuries and recoveries are poised to reshape the MLB postseason picture, with nearly every contender juggling critical absences and fragile returns. - Houston shuts down Carlos Correa after an ankle setback, the Yankees finally get Max Fried and Aaron Judge back, while Shohei Ohtani looms as the Dodgers’ biggest question. Carlos Correa is out. Max Fried is back. Shohei Ohtani is somewhere in between. And questions linger ov
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- As October approaches, injuries and recoveries are poised to reshape the MLB postseason picture, with nearly every contender juggling critical absences and fragile returns.
- Houston shuts down Carlos Correa after an ankle setback, the Yankees finally get Max Fried and Aaron Judge back, while Shohei Ohtani looms as the Dodgers’ biggest question.
Carlos Correa is out. Max Fried is back. Shohei Ohtani is somewhere in between. And questions linger over the postseason availability of several other MLB difference-makers as October approaches.
Here is a look at the injury status and hopeful returns of impact players on playoff qualifiers and contenders:
American League East
Tampa Bay Rays: Acquired from Baltimore at the trade deadline, swingman Tyler Wells posted a 1.50 earned-run average before right forearm tightness sidelined him. He is back solely pitching from the bullpen, and could be a key piece for the Rays in their surprising surge to the division title.
Hopeful return: Slick-fielding shortstop Taylor Walls is recovering from a right hip flexor strain and signs point to him returning by October.
The Dodgers clinch a playoff berth with their 4-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds, reaching the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year.
New York Yankees: The return of staff ace Fried is huge for a team that has clinched a wild-card berth and remains a long step behind the Rays for a division title and first-round bye. The left-hander out of Studio City Harvard-Westlake High gave up one run while walking none over seven innings in his longest start in almost five months. Fried has had two arduous IL stints dealing with a bone bruise on his left elbow.
Hopeful returns: Giancarlo Stanton or Trent Grisham returning in October would give the Yankees lineup additional pop. Three-time AL MVP Aaron Judge has been back for a week since missing more than three months with a fractured rib.
Boston Red Sox: A right quadriceps strain has kept All-Star center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela sidelined for two weeks. However, Rafaela told NESN that he expects to be activated this weekend, a substantial addition to a team that likely will play the Yankees in wild-card series.
Hopeful return: A year ago, Garrett Crochet was 18-5 and led the AL with 205 1/3 innings pitched. This year, left shoulder inflammation and a lat strain have kept him sidelined since April. However, he has ramped up bullpen sessions and is targeting a postseason return as a reliever.
American League Central
Chicago White Sox: The most improved team in baseball is desperately trying to hold off the Guardians and win a division title after finishing last two years in a row. Chicago has enjoyed good health and added journeyman outfielder Tommy Pham from the Phillies on Aug. 31. Pham was activated from the IL on Wednesday and could provide valuable postseason experience to complement his young new teammates — he has hit .315 in 37 career playoff games.
Hopeful return: Drew Thorpe was reinstated from the 60-day IL on Wednesday and is an intriguing option. The right-hander from Cal Poly SLO was a key piece in the 2024 trade that sent Dylan Cease to the Padres but has spent nearly two full seasons on the shelf. Now healthy, his inclusion on the playoff roster would be a gamble that his elite stuff can mask his inexperience.
Cleveland Guardians: Jo Adell didn’t come off the IL, but the addition of the former confounding Angels prospect in an August salary dump has bolstered the Guardians’ outfield — long a problem area. Adell has driven in 28 runs in 38 games with Cleveland and joins glittering rookie Chase DeLauter and steady veteran Steven Kwan in a productive outfield.
Hopeful return: Reliever Shawn Armstrong, who signed a one-year, $5.5-million contract last offseason, has been sidelined since July 24 with a calf strain. Barring a setback in his final minor league rehab appearance, he could be activated in time for the playoffs.
American League West
Houston Astros: Correa, whose second act with Houston has been a flop because of injuries, was working on an accelerated comeback from May ankle surgery. A few days ago, team officials expressed optimism, but Tuesday they decided to shelve their shortstop when the ankle became inflamed after a workout. Houston is clinging to a one-game lead over the Texas Rangers in the AL West.
Hopeful return: Nothing of note.
Texas Rangers: Still in contention despite spending much of the season under .500, the Rangers welcomed back pitcher Nathan Eovaldi and third baseman Josh Jung from the injured list over the weekend. A calf strain had kept Jung sidelined since July 21 and Eovaldi had been out since Aug. 7 with elbow inflammation. Eovaldi, who has started in all but 20 of his 339 MLB appearances, will pitch out of the bullpen.
Hopeful return: Nothing of note.
National League East
Atlanta Braves: Reynaldo López inflated hopes of a late-career surge when he posted a 1.99 ERA over 25 starts in his first season with Atlanta. But injuries — including right shoulder inflammation this season — have severely limited his contribution. López was placed on the IL again Tuesday.
Hopeful return: Bryce Elder had an arthroscopic procedure to clean up bone fragments in his right knee on Sept. 8. The hope is that the right-handed starter can recover quickly enough to be counted upon in the postseason.
By not putting Shohei Ohtani on the injured list in July or in August, the Dodgers may have compromised the two-way star’s ability to be healthy for the playoffs.
Philadelphia Phillies: Although an MRI found no structural damage to the throwing shoulder of stalwart starter Jesús Luzardo, the left-hander remains a question for the playoffs. He was placed on the 15-day IL retroactive to Sept. 12, and it is doubtful he could pitch again in the regular season. Luzardo has a 2.87 ERA across 29 starts this season.
Hopeful return: Tanner Banks, a major contributor to the Philadelphia bullpen in 2025, was reinstated from the 60-day IL over the weekend. Although he wasn’t effective earlier this season, Banks is welcomed back because Phillies relievers have been poor against left-handed hitters.
National League Central
Milwaukee Brewers: Huntington Beach Marina High product Jake Bauers has suffered from shin splints almost all season, and the pain has kept him from playing the outfield lately. He can play first base, but that takes slugger Andrew Vaughn out of the lineup. Bauers, with 26 home runs and 83 RBIs, has been a key bat for Milwaukee. He has been particularly tough against the Dodgers, batting .348 with a .483 on-base percentage.
Hopeful return: Brandon Woodruff, one of the best starters in baseball when healthy, is rehabbing from shoulder inflammation that sidelined him in July. The Brewers are nearly guaranteed a first-round bye, giving Woodruff an extra week to build stamina.
Chicago Cubs: Shortstop and team leader Dansby Swanson will be welcomed back after missing a month with a left oblique injury. He is expected to rejoin the Cubs during their weekend series against the Cincinnati Reds.
Hopeful return: Left-handed starter Justin Steele is progressing through bullpen sessions and is almost ready to take the mound after missing the entire season with a left elbow flexor strain. Steele, whose record was 16-5 in 2023, likely would pitch from the bullpen in the postseason.
National League West
Dodgers: The loss of center fielder Andy Pages is significant. He can bat near the top or bottom of the order, displays power and speed, and had improved his patience at the plate enough to earn a career-high 45 walks in 128 games.
Hopeful return: Getting Ohtani healthy enough to produce at the plate is a priority, and his absence from the mound shouldn’t be felt if Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tarik Skubal and Tyler Glasnow pitch to their capabilities. Meanwhile, Edwin Diaz might not even make the playoff roster.
Edwin Díaz struggled in his rehab start Sunday, and Dave Roberts is making it clear the Dodgers “got to see something” before putting him on the playoff roster.
San Diego Padres: While recovering from Tommy John surgery, starter Joe Musgrove made it a goal to be ready for the postseason. Recovery difficulties between starts have made his status doubtful, however. Nick Pivetta, on the other hand, has pitched well in two starts since coming off the IL and appears ready.
Hopeful return: Ramón Laureano, a 2025 trade deadline acquisition with a potent bat, last played May 30 because of hip inflammation. However, he told reporters that the chances of him playing in the postseason are “less than 5%.”
Arizona Diamondbacks: Zac Gallen was activated from the 60-day IL and Michael Soroka from the 15-day IL, giving the Diamondbacks two starters in their push to win a wild-card berth. Gallen, a proven starter who has been horrendous in 2026, has been out since the All-Star break with elbow inflammation. Soroka was out only two weeks with the same ailment.
Hopeful return: Third baseman Nolan Arenado suffered an injury to his left thumb Tuesday, the same injury he sustained in late August. It’s doubtful the injury would sideline the 14-year veteran with games this week being so important, yet the Diamondbacks have to hope the injury doesn’t impact his productivity.

item.title: [BroBible] The Original Photo Used To Create The 1952 Topps Mickey Mantle Card Shattered A Price Record After Being Auctioned Off
item.dc:creator: Colin Witte
item.description: Collectors have spent decades paying increasingly ridiculous amounts of money for Mickey Mantle’s iconic 1952 Topps card, so apparently the hobby eventually had to work backward to the thing that existed before the cardboard. The original photograph Topps used to create the card’s famous image just sold privately for $3 million. The 7-by-9-inch black-and-white photograph was taken during Yankees spring training in Phoenix on March 5, 1951, months before Mantle made his major-league debut. Hunt A
item.content:encoded:
Collectors have spent decades paying increasingly ridiculous amounts of money for Mickey Mantle’s iconic 1952 Topps card, so apparently the hobby eventually had to work backward to the thing that existed before the cardboard. The original photograph Topps used to create the card’s famous image just sold privately for $3 million.
The 7-by-9-inch black-and-white photograph was taken during Yankees spring training in Phoenix on March 5, 1951, months before Mantle made his major-league debut. Hunt Auctions brokered the private transaction, with Sports Collectors Daily reporting the price established a record for a Type I sports photograph.
The Cardboard Is Not Even The Most Interesting Part Anymore
This was basically the raw material for one of the most recognizable baseball cards ever made.
International News Service originally distributed the photo regionally rather than nationally, which helped make surviving originals extremely scarce. Topps later used Mantle’s portrait as the basis for the painted image on card No. 311 in its 1952 set.
The photograph carries PSA’s coveted Type I classification, which means it was developed from the original negative within roughly two years of the image being taken. PSA considers Type I examples the most desirable category because they are first-generation photographs created closest to the moment itself.
Only a handful of Type I versions of this particular Mantle image are known, which apparently makes $3 million sound reasonable to somebody.
The same kind of photograph sold for $375,000 in 2019. Another Type I image, the photograph used for his actual 1951 Bowman rookie card, sold for $843,750 in 2024, which made it the most expensive one ever sold in the category.
Now the 1952 Topps source photo has essentially taken that market and launched it into another tax bracket.
The Buyer Also Owns A $12.6 Million Card
Here is where this turns from expensive collecting into assembling the world’s most ridiculous before-and-after set.
The buyer was commercial real-estate investor Ron Firman, who also owns the famous SGC Mint+ 9.5 example of the 1952 Topps Mantle that Heritage sold for $12.6 million in 2022.
So one collector now owns both the photograph and the cardboard masterpiece it helped create. Combined purchase price: $15.6 million.
There is also a funny distinction worth making whenever the 1952 Mantle comes up. Despite frequently being called a rookie card, Mantle’s recognized rookie was issued by Bowman in 1951. The 1952 version was his first Topps card and simply became so famous that it eventually swallowed almost everything else connected to his collecting market.
Now even the source material is worth more than most pieces of luxury real estate.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are set to wrap up their series with the Minnesota Twins on Wednesday afternoon.
If they win on Wednesday, New York will complete the sweep of the Twins and head into the next series (out West against the Diamondbacks) with some important momentum.
Before the Twins series finale, the Yanks revealed their lineup, which features several changes and a notable Jose Caballero decision.
More MLB on Heavy: Toronto Blue Jays Announce Brandon Valenzuela News to Salvage Tigers Series
Jose Caballero OUT of Yankees Batting Order on Wednesday
After playing the last three games for the Yankees, Jose Caballero will get a day off for the series finale with the Twins.
Instead, Anthony Volpe is playing 2B and batting ninth. Caballero has been bouncing around between third base and second recently.
Per @UnderdogMLB, here is the full Yankees order:
Yankees 9/16: "B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF A. Judge RF L. García Jr. 1B S. Jones CF G. Lombard Jr. SS R. McMahon 3B A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B C. Rodón SP"
Aaron Judge is back in the order, and Austin Wells is as well.
More MLB on Heavy: Pete Alonso Trolls New York Mets Fans By Sending Clear Orioles Message
Taking a Quick Look at Jose Caballero This Season
In his second season in Pinstripes, Jose Caballero is batting .234 with 14 home runs, 50 RBI, and an OPS+ of 84.
The thing that keeps Caballero in the lineup is his defensive versatility, as he's been able to play all across the diamond for the Yanks.
His bWAR is solid at 2.3 because of his defensive prowess, which is an impressive mark.
It's unclear if Jose Caballero will be a part of the October fold for New York, as that will likely depend on who is swinging the best bat at the time.

item.title: [southshorepress.com] Spencer Jones Has Arrived — And the Yankees Better Notice
item.dc:creator: The South Shore Press; Tom Barton
item.description: Spencer Jones Has Arrived — And the Yankees Better Notice For anyone who might have doubted it, let’s be perfectly clear: Spencer Jones has arrived. The highly touted Yankees prospect came through the minor leagues with some major question marks. His large stature and concerns about his hit tool led some to wonder whether he would ever consistently make enough contact to become an everyday player. But the athletic ability and big-time power were always enticing enough for the Yankees to give him
item.content:encoded:
Spencer Jones Has Arrived — And the Yankees Better Notice
For anyone who might have doubted it, let’s be perfectly clear: Spencer Jones has arrived.
The highly touted Yankees prospect came through the minor leagues with some major question marks. His large stature and concerns about his hit tool led some to wonder whether he would ever consistently make enough contact to become an everyday player.
But the athletic ability and big-time power were always enticing enough for the Yankees to give him his opportunity.
During his first stint in the majors, the strikeout issues were certainly noticeable, and the questions only got louder. Could Jones really handle a full-time role? Were there simply too many holes in his swing?
Well, we can officially put those questions to rest.
Because Jones has taken off.
Jones is batting .346 with five home runs and a .933 OPS over his last 25 games. He is also hitting over .300 with an OPS above .900 over his last 35 games.
And the best part may be yet to come.
Jones is batting a ridiculous .435 with a 1.251 OPS against left-handed pitching this season, both lead MLB (min 50 PA).
That number should get everyone’s attention.
There were questions about whether Jones might eventually become a platoon player or fall into the dreaded “three true outcomes” category — a player whose game revolves around home runs, walks and strikeouts.
Instead, we are seeing something much more complete.
Jones brings excellent defense and the ability to run, along with the power that made him such an intriguing prospect in the first place. When you put all of that together, you are looking at a player who is beginning to look an awful lot like a true five-tool talent.
And that changes things for the Yankees.
When Trent Grisham returns, there will be decisions to make. But after watching what Jones has done lately, there should be no more wondering whether he belongs in the conversation.
Spencer Jones has answered the questions the best way a baseball player can.
He has gone out and hit.
Now, let’s hope the Yankees, and Aaron Boone, realize what they have.

item.title: [sportingnews.com] Jazz Chisholm Jr. urged to accept $21.05M offer if Yankees make it | Sporting News
item.dc:creator: Matt Sullivan
item.description: The New York Yankees are facing a big decision with infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr. this offseason. He's set to hit the open market, and finding someone as talented as him might be hard to come by. But he had a down 2026 season, and it would not be a huge surprise if the Yankees decided to pick someone else to upgrade their infield. However, Chisholm might have the ball in his court this offseason if the Yankees extend the qualifying offer. Bleacher Report's Tim Kelly is urging Chisholm to accept th
item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are facing a big decision with infielder Jazz Chisholm Jr. this offseason. He's set to hit the open market, and finding someone as talented as him might be hard to come by.
But he had a down 2026 season, and it would not be a huge surprise if the Yankees decided to pick someone else to upgrade their infield. However, Chisholm might have the ball in his court this offseason if the Yankees extend the qualifying offer.
Bleacher Report's Tim Kelly is urging Chisholm to accept that $21.05 million qualifying offer if the Yankees extend it, as his down 2026 season might lead to a weaker free agent market, and Chisholm could look to prove he's worth more for next offseason.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. urged to accept qualifying offer from Yankees if they extend it
"If the Yankees extend a qualifying offer to Chisholm - which was worth $21.05 million last offseason - the 28-year-old would probably be wise to take it and hope for a rebound season in 2027," Kelly writes.
While Chisholm could hit the open market after the 2026 season and seek out a long-term deal, his mediocre at-best 2026 season might result in a weaker free agent market.
He's currently on the injured list and is making $10.16 million this season. If he were playing at his best ability, he'd easily double that contract value on a long-term deal.
But instead, the infielder has 1.4 bWAR this season across 134 games with a .715 OPS and 98 OPS+, the lowest and second-lowest marks of his MLB career, respectively.
Seeking out a large multi-year deal worth north of $20 million per-year after such a season isn't very likely. While he's bound to receive interest, it's not likely to be the kind of deal he really wants to accept.
Instead, if he accepts the one-year qualifying offer from the Yankees, which would be somewhere around $21.05 million, he could wind up landing a massive new deal during the 2027-2028 free agency if he has a strong 2027 season.
It's a risk for Chisholm, but if he's willing to bet on himself putting up more similar numbers to his 2025 season with a 122 OPS+, then Chisholm should listen to Kelly's urging and take the qualifying offer if the Yankees extend it.

item.title: [theleadsm.com] Cam Schlittler Has a Strong Case for MVP
item.dc:creator: James Nolan
item.description: The American League Cy Young race is over. In his last start, Cam Schlittler twirled a six-inning, one-hit, eight-strikeout gem against the Mets. In fact, ESPN’s award tracker no longer has odds for the race. With the Yankees also clinching a playoff berth with their win Monday night, there’s not much left at stake in New York’s regular season. Except for Schlittler’s potential run at being the first pitcher to win MVP since 2014. Schlittler has two starts remaining this year. Barring Aaron Boon
item.content:encoded:
The American League Cy Young race is over. In his last start, Cam Schlittler twirled a six-inning, one-hit, eight-strikeout gem against the Mets. In fact, ESPN’s award tracker no longer has odds for the race.
With the Yankees also clinching a playoff berth with their win Monday night, there’s not much left at stake in New York’s regular season. Except for Schlittler’s potential run at being the first pitcher to win MVP since 2014.
Schlittler has two starts remaining this year. Barring Aaron Boone toying with the rotation to line them up for the postseason, he’s scheduled to get the ball for game two in Arizona on Sept. 19 and game four against the Rays on Sept. 24.
The Statistical Case
There’s a long list of stats you can cite to put Schlittler’s dominance this season in context. There are a few worth highlighting.
Schlittler’s ERA is currently an AL-best 1.95. That’s the lowest ERA of any qualified Yankees starter since Ron Guidry (1.74)in 1978. The next most recent sub-two ERA in Yankee history is 1943 Spud Chandler (1.64). He also has a marginally better ERA than Jacob Misiorowski, the NL frontrunner for Cy Young.
While they both display a 1.95 ERA, the formula for ERA actually allows for the
Schlittler also has a better ERA+ than .
ERA+ adjusts to the league, wherein league average is always 100. That means Schlittler has been 116% better than league average, while Kershaw was “only” 97% better. Schlittler has also done this in 31 starts, while Kershaw has done it in only 27.
Finally, he currently leads the American League in Wins Above Replacement. Yordan Alvarez (5.8), the odds-on favorite, Junior Caminero (5.3), the home run leader, and Bobby Witt Jr. (6.3) all trail Schlittler’s mark of 7.1. In an award measuring value, Schlittler has statistically impacted his team the most.
The last time a pitcher won MVP was Kershaw in 2014. Spud Chandler also won in 1943, and Guidry finished second in 1978.
The Comparative Case
The American League MVP race at this point is down to five names. Schlittler, Alvarez, Caminero, Witt Jr. and rookie sensation Kevin McGonigle.
Players like Ben Rice and Dillon Dingler were in the thick of the race, but recently played themselves out with .641 and .518 OPS in August, respectively.
Yordan Alvarez
Alvarez is still the favorite, per ESPN. He currently leads baseball in on-base percentage (.427) and slugging percentage (.589), and the American League in batting average (.310). Since his debut in 2019, he has done nothing but mash at the plate, with 2026 his best and healthiest season yet.
It’s hard enough for a primary DH to win MVP. Of course, Ohtani’s done it four of the last five years, but Alvarez isn’t stealing 50 bases or throwing 100 innings. In fact, .
He’s also been abysmal down the stretch. Over the last calendar month (Aug. 15 – Sept. 15) he’s slashed just .238/.375/.393 with two homers and eight RBI. He was once poised to run away with the triple crown, and now it looks like a long shot.
The triple crown is Alvarez’s best bet. If he can turn around these remaining 12 games and reclaim the home run and RBI title, his case is as good as gold. As it stands, Alvarez and Rice are tied for second with 38 home runs to Caminero’s 40. Pete Alonso leads the way with 100 runs driven in, with Alvarez (96) and Caminero (95) close behind.
Junior Caminero
Caminero has been phenomenal in just his 22-year-old season. He’s one of the league’s premier sluggers, hitting 40 homers in 2025 and 2026. He’s a cornerstone on the first-place Tampa Bay Rays.
The main argument against Caminero mirrors Alvarez’s: his game is very one-dimensional. While his hitting prowess is undeniable, he is a negative asset on the base paths and at third base. Unlike Alvarez, he hasn’t cooled off in the final weeks of summer, but at no point this season has he had a narrative driving his MVP case home.
Caminero would surely be a worthy winner. He is a three-true-outcome generator; his batting average sits at a respectable .279.
Bobby Witt Jr.
Then there’s Bobby Witt Jr. He finished second in voting in 2024 and fourth in 2025. He’s perhaps the most well-rounded five -tool player in the league. His game really has no weakness.
2026 could be classified as a “down-year” for him, with “only” a .280 batting average and 18 home runs. He missed about two weeks toward the end of July, so his counting stats aren’t in their usual spot. He doesn’t lead the league in batting, stolen bases, or hits as he has in years past.
He’ll undoubtedly finish towards the top of the ballot, but it’s hard to imagine voters choosing 2026 to reward him. His fifth-place Royals also won’t help his case, especially against the Yankees, Rays and Astros, all currently in a playoff position.
Kevin McGonigle
McGonigle’s rookie season has been excellent. He has split time at shortstop and third base for the Tigers. His offensive profile fits a seasoned veteran. An incredibly balanced slash line of .273/.373/.425 with a nearly even ratio of strikeouts (89) to walks (88). His 6.6 WAR leads position players, but an MLB rookie has only won MVP twice, and not since Ichiro Suzuki in 2001.
It’s hard to imagine a world where McGonigle finds his way atop the voting. Like Witt, he does not lead in any statistical category. His first season in the big leagues has been great, and it’s not far-fetched to say he will take home the award one day, but he will probably finish fifth or sixth in 2026.
Case Closed?
While Aaron Boone endorses his ace as the MVP, teammate and three-time MVP Aaron Judge doesn’t.
“They’ve got a Cy Young Award for a reason, best pitcher in the game. He’s got my vote, definitely, for the Cy Young,” Judge said.
Ultimately, the final two weeks of the season carry a lot of weight. If Yordan Alvarez can turn his bat back on and secure the triple crown, Schlittler stands no chance. If he stays cool and Schlittler has two strong outings left in him, then it might be time to see baseball’s next MVP pitcher.

Jones broke the game open in the sixth inning with a three-run blast to center field that gave the Yankees a 7-1 lead. The 25-year-old had a quiet start to his MLB career, posting a .739 OPS across 65 games through the end of August. item.content:encoded:
Jones went 1-for-5 with a three-run home run against the Twins in an 8-1 victory Tuesday.
Jones broke the game open in the sixth inning with a three-run blast to center field that gave the Yankees a 7-1 lead. The 25-year-old had a quiet start to his MLB career, posting a .739 OPS across 65 games through the end of August. However, Jones has come alive in September, slashing .340/.415/.532 with two homers, 12 RBI, seven runs and one stolen base through his first 13 contests this month. He's still striking out too much -- Jones has a 34.0 percent strikeout rate in September and a 35.0 percent punchout rate overall this season -- but he's become New York's everyday center fielder, starting each of the Yankees' past 14 games at that position.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] New York Yankees @ Minnesota Twins: Carlos Rodón vs. Zebby Matthews
item.dc:creator: Jeremy Nielsen
item.description: It's been a nice start to the week in the Yankees' home-away-from-home. On Monday night, they clinched a postseason berth with a 7-3 win against the Twins. On Tuesday evening, they fielded the proverbial "hangover lineup" of sorts and still cruised to an 8-1 victory behind a strong start from Max Fried and plenty of strong performances at the plate. item.content:encoded:
It's been a nice start to the week in the Yankees' home-away-from-home. On Monday night, they clinched a postseason berth with a 7-3 win against the Twins. On Tuesday evening, they fielded the proverbial "hangover lineup" of sorts and still cruised to an 8-1 victory behind a strong start from Max Fried and plenty of strong performances at the plate.
On today's getaway day game in Minneapolis, Carlos Rodón leads the Yankees' effort for a sweep. His most recent start against the Mets was perhaps the best of his season, as he held down the crosstown rivals for one run in 6.1 innings—with eight strikeouts to just one walk. For Rodón, who has for various reasons not pitched deep into games as routinely as he did in 2025, a second straight start of six or more innings would be an excellent sign as he prepares for the postseason.
The Twins, now 4-9 in September, will look to young righty Zebby Matthews, who has turned in an uneven campaign on the hill this season. His past three starts have been illustrative of the step-forward-step-back tendency which has tormented many a young hurler. On August 30th, he twirled an absolute gem, pitching into the ninth inning against the rival White Sox with just one run allowed in a win. His next appearance, also against Chicago, was a far more pedestrian five-inning, four-run effort. Then last time out, he failed to escape the third inning in Detroit—walking four batters and surrendering five runs to hit the showers early.
While the Yankees rested a few of their starters for last night's contest, including Aaron Judge, it didn't prevent them from running up the score. Today, Judge returns to the lineup card, hitting third behind DH Ben Rice and Cody Bellinger, who led the way with three hits and a homer last night. Cleanup hitter Luis García Jr., Spencer Jones, and George Lombard Jr. will make up the middle of the order, with Ryan McMahon, Austin Wells, and second baseman Anthony Volpe (it's still weird to say that) pulling up the rear.

item.content:encoded:
WHITE PLAINS, Nueva York.— El legendario Mariano Rivera volvió a reunir este martes a grandes figuras del deporte, empresarios, profesionales y líderes comunitarios durante la celebración del cuarto torneo de golf de su Fundación, una jornada que combinó deporte, amistad y solidaridad en beneficio de niños y jóvenes de comunidades desatendidas.
El evento de este año llevó oficialmente el nombre de Mariano Rivera Save 653 Invitational 2026 y tuvo como escenario el prestigioso Metropolis Country Club, en White Plains, Nueva York.
La actividad se desarrolló durante todo el martes 15 de septiembre, con una programación que incluyó golf, confraternidad y una gala benéfica.
Uno de los principales respaldos de la jornada fue el de Gorayeb & Associates, P.C., firma conocida como “los abogados del pueblo”, que fue designada patrocinador principal del invitacional.
La firma tiene entre sus áreas de trabajo la representación de trabajadores lesionados y casos relacionados con accidentes de construcción.
El respaldo de Gorayeb & Associates estuvo representado en el torneo por Chris Gorayeb, presidente de la firma; su hijo Jay Gorayeb, y Marlon Mazo, quienes compartieron con Rivera y con las numerosas personalidades que participaron en esta importante actividad.
La jornada también contó con la presencia de tres reconocidas figuras del pitcheo de las Grandes Ligas: Orlando “El Duque” Hernández, Dellin Betances y Bartolo Colón, quienes disfrutaron del ambiente creado alrededor del torneo y de la oportunidad de acompañar a Rivera en su iniciativa benéfica.
Entre los invitados especiales también estuvo el doctor Ramón Tallaj, de SOMOS Community Care, además de otras destacadas personalidades de los ámbitos empresarial, deportivo, profesional y comunitario.
El programa comenzó a las 8:30 de la mañana con el registro de los jugadores y el brunch, seguido a las 11:00 a. m. por la salida oficial del torneo, mediante un formato de salida simultánea.
Posteriormente, los participantes regresaron para continuar con las actividades de la tarde.
La parte social de la jornada incluyó una recepción de cóctel, seguida de la cena de gala, entrega de premios y subasta, convirtiendo el encuentro deportivo en una completa jornada de recaudación y apoyo a los programas de la Fundación Mariano Rivera.
Más allá de la competencia en los campos de golf, el verdadero propósito del encuentro estuvo relacionado con la misión de la Fundación.
Los fondos generados por el evento respaldan programas dirigidos a jóvenes de comunidades desatendidas, con iniciativas enfocadas en mentoría, educación, habilidades para la vida, preparación profesional y oportunidades para construir un futuro con mayores posibilidades.
La Fundación Mariano Rivera explica que sus programas buscan proporcionar a niños y jóvenes las herramientas necesarias para superar barreras y avanzar hacia mejores oportunidades educativas y profesionales.
Según información de la propia Fundación difundida con motivo del invitacional, sus iniciativas han impactado a más de 50,000 jóvenes desde su creación.
El Save 653 Invitational volvió así a convertir el nombre de Mariano Rivera en un punto de encuentro entre el deporte de alto nivel y el compromiso social.
El histórico ex cerrador de los Yankees, miembro del Salón de la Fama del Béisbol, continúa llevando fuera del terreno los valores que marcaron su carrera profesional.
La presencia de figuras como El Duque Hernández, Betances y Colón, junto a Chris y Jay Gorayeb, Marlon Mazo, Ramón Tallaj y numerosas personalidades, le dio al cuarto torneo una dimensión especial y reforzó el carácter de confraternidad que ha acompañado esta iniciativa.
Para Mariano Rivera, cada edición del torneo representa una oportunidad para reunir a sus amigos, antiguos colegas y colaboradores alrededor de una causa que tiene como centro a los jóvenes y sus posibilidades de construir un mejor futuro.
El Mariano Rivera Save 653 Invitational 2026 cerró así una nueva jornada en la que el golf sirvió como vehículo para la solidaridad, mientras el respaldo de Gorayeb & Associates y la presencia de destacadas figuras de las Grandes Ligas contribuyeron al éxito de una actividad concebida para dejar beneficios mucho más allá del campo de golf.

item.title: [Just Baseball] Cam Schlittler Has Wrapped Up the AL Cy Young Race | Just Baseball
item.dc:creator: Cade Lalim
item.description: Postseason baseball is right around the corner, which means it’s time to analyze a certain starting pitcher who seems to have American League Cy Young honors pretty much wrapped up with a bow. I’m talking about New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler, who’s in the midst of an incredibly successful second season in the majors and looks like he’ll be a force in the league for a long time. After former Detroit Tigers star Tarik Skubal walked away with the American League Cy Young in both 2024 and 2025,
item.content:encoded:
Postseason baseball is right around the corner, which means it’s time to analyze a certain starting pitcher who seems to have American League Cy Young honors pretty much wrapped up with a bow.
I’m talking about New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler, who’s in the midst of an incredibly successful second season in the majors and looks like he’ll be a force in the league for a long time.
After former Detroit Tigers star Tarik Skubal walked away with the American League Cy Young in both 2024 and 2025, Schlittler is looking to assert himself as the new frontline pitcher in the American League. Let’s just say if Skubal didn’t get traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers and still remained on the Detroit Tigers, Schlittler probably still would have the upper hand, which is pretty impressive.
Other elite arms like Dylan Cease, Parker Messick, Drew Rasmussen and Reid Detmers have certainly given him a run for his money, but Schlittler is likely to take home the hardware when it’s all said and done.
He is also looking to be the Yankees’ second Cy Young Award winner in the last four years. Gerrit Cole took home the honors in 2023 after his excellent campaign, in which he owned a 2.63 ERA and 0.98 WHIP. Schlittler’s 2026 campaign has actually been even better.
Now that everything has been set up, it’s time to dig deeper into what has fueled Schlittler’s elite 2026 campaign.
*Stats pulled from games completed through September 14.
Schlittler Came Out of the Blue, Kind Of
Up until the 2025 season, most people probably didn’t even know who Cam Schlittler was and what organization he was a part of. He was drafted by the Yankees in the seventh round of the 2022 draft out of Northeastern University.
He was an all-around solid pitcher in college over his three seasons, posting a 2.62 ERA and 1.08 WHIP, with 30 out of his 31 appearances being starts.
Schlittler didn’t make his affiliated debut within the Yankees system until the 2023 season and showed mixed results between rookie ball, Single-A, and High-A.
Even though he struck out a lot of batters and kept home runs to a minimum, he issued a lot of walks, which inflated his surface numbers.
Over the next two years spanning the 2024 and 2025 seasons, he gradually made his way through the Yankees’ minor league system and started to show some solid improvements.
By the time the 2025 campaign rolled around, Schlittler found himself on MLB Pipeline’s list of the Yankees’ top 30 prospects for the first time, being slotted in at number 12.
He was mowing down hitters, limiting walks, limiting home runs and was simply putting it all together between Double-A and Triple-A.
| Season | HR/9 | BB/9 | K/9 |
| 2023 | 0.8 | 4.1 | 9.8 |
| 2024 | 0.7 | 4.1 | 11.5 |
| 2025 | 0.5 | 3.1 | 11.6 |
Schlittler’s excellent performance was evident to the Yankees front office, and the organization decided it was time to give him a shot at the major league level. Let’s just say it’s been stunning to see what he’s been able to accomplish so quickly.
Pure Dominance in the Majors
Now that I’ve highlighted Schlittler’s underlooked journey to the big leagues, hopefully you’ll appreciate his insane numbers a little more and notice how far he has come along in terms of development.
He had a nice cup of tea with the Yankees in 2025 after he debuted on July 9, finishing the season with an excellent 2.96 ERA and 1.22 WHIP spanning a stretch of 14 starts. A majority of his growth in the minor leagues had carried over to the majors, which was really encouraging to see.
Last year, Schlittler gave us a little glimpse into what he’d provide long term, but no one realized what kind of pitching monster he’d turn into presently in 2026.
You could even argue that he’s been better than Jacob Misiorowski because their numbers have pretty much been identical, give or take. That means you could argue he’s the best pitcher in the majors currently.
So far in 2026, across 31 starts and 184.2 innings pitched, Schlittler has shown pure dominance, pitching to a superb 1.95 ERA and 0.90 WHIP. His ratios have been really good, as backed up by his excellent 6 H/9, 0.8 HR/9, 2.1 BB/9 and 11.1 K/9.
Schlittler currently leads the American League with 5.9 fWAR. He ranks second overall, only trailing Misirowski, who has been worth 6.0 fWAR.
His underlying peripherals look great, including his 2.87 xERA and 2.57 FIP. That is a result of his ability to limit dangerous contact and total baserunners via low hit and walk rates, as previously mentioned.
In terms of pitching run value calculated by Baseball Savant, Schlittler ranks fourth in the majors, currently worth +38 runs. He trails only Yoshinobu Yamamoto (39), Dylan Cease (39) and Jacob Misiorowski (47).
The reason as to why his pitching run value is so high is because of how effective his pitch arsenal has been. Schlittler primarily works with four quality pitches: a four-seam fastball (44%), cutter (25%), sinker (20%) and curveball (10%).
The fastball combo of his four-seam and sinker has been lethal and goes to show how important and effective tunneling can be.
Schlittler’s fastball, which averages 98 mph, is worth a +27 run value, and batters have only managed a .164 batting average and .230 wOBA against the offering. His counterpart 97.8 mph sinker is being valued at a +11 run value, with a .172 batting average and .266 xwOBA.
Also note that Schlittler has 6.8 feet of extension, which places him in the 81st percentile. This helps create a faster perceived velocity for an already powerful fastball mix.
His cutter, which averages 94.7 mph, has been a hint above average with a +1 run value, while his 86.3 mph curveball has been his worst and least-used pitch, worth -1 in run value. If Schlittler can improve just one of those pitches, it could be wraps for his opponents.
Schlittler’s stuff has been very good, to say the least, and batters are having a really hard time making contact on his offerings. His current 34.2% chase rate ranks in the 85th percentile, while his 29.1% whiff rate ranks in the 79th percentile.
Despite the fact that opponents are making limited contact with Schlittler’s offerings, they still have managed to make decent contact when they do connect.
This is one of the few flaws in Schlittler’s already great profile that could use some improvement. Opponents have managed a 7.7% barrel rate (45th percentile) and 39.1% hard-hit (44th percentile) rate against him. Those numbers aren’t bad, but they could be better.
Will Schlittler Take Home AL Cy Young Honors?
Plain and simple, Schlittler has been dominant. And there’s actually a good chance he gets even better down the road based on what we’ve looked at.
It seems very likely that Schlittler will be named the 2026 American League Cy Young when it’s all said and done. Cease has pleaded his case in the best way he’s able to, but all signs are pointing to Schlittler.
Simply just looking at Schlittler’s and Cease’s second-half splits pretty much ends the conversation.
Yordan Alvarez seems like the leading candidate for American League Most Valuable Player, but you’d think Schlittler will be considered there as well. Alvarez leads all AL batters with 5.8 fWAR, but Schlittler does have him topped with 5.9 fWAR — something to keep an eye out for.
We’ll have to wait and see what happens, but Schlittler looks to have wrapped up the conversation for the American League Cy Young.

item.title: [Pinstripe Alley] Yankees activate Clarke Schmidt, designate Oswaldo Cabrera for assignment
item.dc:creator: Jake Devin

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees reinstated Clarke Schmidt from the 60-day injured list ahead of today’s series finale in Minnesota. The team also optioned right-handed reliever Bradley Hanner to Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, and designated Oswaldo Cabrera for assignment.
It’s the end of a long road back for Schmidt, who hasn’t pitched on a major league mound since July 2025 after undergoing Tommy John surgery. At the time, Schmidt was in the midst of establishing himself as one of the Yankees’ best starters, running a 3.07 ERA across 164 innings between 2024 and 2025.
Schmidt won’t have enough time to build up to a starter’s workload prior to the postseason, but he has a real chance to make an impact in the Yankee bullpen. He’s been used in one-to-two inning stretches in the minors, where his fastball has sat around his customary 94 mph. Beyond David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, and Brent Headrick, the Yankees have little set in stone in their bullpen, leaving a wide opportunity for someone like Schmidt to grab a meaningful role with a strong showing in the final two weeks of the season.
The Yankees had to manage their 40-man roster as a result of this move, and Cabrera was sadly the casualty. Schmidt coming off the 60-day IL necessitated clearing a spot on a full 40-man. Cabrera, who has spent most of the season at Triple-A after recovering from a gruesome knee injury last year, drew the short stick. The Yankees could have plausibly transferred Fernando Cruz to the 60-day IL, but instead opted to keep hope alive for a return from Cruz.

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees’ pitching picture continues to regain its health, as Clarke Schmidt was reinstated from the 60-day injured list on Wednesday as he returns from Tommy John surgery.
The 30-year-old right-hander had been out since July 3 of last season when he was diagnosed with a torn UCL that not only required Tommy John surgery, but also an internal brace procedure. He had a 3.32 ERA and a 1.090 WHIP in 14 starts last season before the injury
He should be in play for a full-time spot in the rotation next season. Over 30 starts between the 2024 and 2025 seasons, he sported a 3.07 ERA and a 1.140 WHIP, which would make an already-great starting five that much more elite.
In the immediate future, though, Schmidt will likely spend this upcoming postseason in the bullpen. Shortened rotations would likely see the Yankees roll with four starters, and there is no usurping Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, or Carlos Rodon.
To make room for him on the 40-man roster, the Yankees designated utilityman Oswaldo Cabrera for assignment. He played just three games with the big-league club this season, spending most of his time with Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre. The 27-year-old was slashing .288/.345/.444 in 122 games, but owned a .635 career OPS across parts of five seasons with the Yankees.

item.content:encoded:
Spencer Jones and Aaron Judge had very different seasons as 25-year-olds for the New York Yankees. When Judge's season finished in 2016, it looked like he could be in the future plans, but he still had to compete with Aaron Hicks in spring training the following season. Things might be a little different for Jones, though. It's hard to imagine the center field job not being his next year, or the Yankees even having to find somebody to compete with him next spring.
This season, Jones is hitting .259/.331/.452 with 10 home runs, 37 RBI, and nine stolen bases. What's great about Jones's production is that it isn't a small sample, either. He has done it over 250 plate appearances.
If the Yankees had any thoughts about retaining Trent Grisham or finding a center fielder on the open market, that really shouldn't be a need anymore. Where else are they getting the production Jones is giving them?
Luis Robert is one name the Yankees could have targeted if things had gone differently with Jones. He has pop in his bat and is one of the speedier outfielders in baseball. Now, they should avoid signing a player like this and allocate resources elsewhere.
Jones' raw tools could make for an exceptional player
While Robert has some power upside, Jones has even more. That's another plus in Jones's column. The rookie's peripherals on the backend suggest an outstanding ability to crush baseballs.
According to Baseball Savant, Jones has an average exit velocity of 94.1 MPH, a 15.7% barrel rate, a 54.7% hard-hit rate, and a lightning-quick 77.2 MPH average bat speed. The Yankees definitely aren't getting a player with that type of raw power on the open market, either.
The issue with Jones is that his defense has been spotty, but when a player can hit like that, they can live with some growing pains. Jones has a -2 Outs Above Average this season, but he could improve. He has the tools there, too.
Jones has 89th-percentile sprint speed and 80th-percentile arm strength. Those are two areas where Grisham has declined (34th-percentile sprint speed and 65th-percentile arm strength), and the one benefit of having Jones in center field is that he can get to balls Grisham otherwise couldn't.
Grisham also has a -6 Outs Above Average this season, which is a notable decline from 2025 (-2), which again speaks to why Jones' growth and continued development in center is important.
Now, it's not to say that Jones will end up being Willie Mays out in center. As long as he's competent, the Yankees will take that. On a given night, he can send a ball 450 feet and change the entire complexion of a ballgame with his power. There were signs of this in the spring, but it's hard to imagine anybody could have predicted this.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees have already clinched the postseason, but still have a lot more to play for as they try to go for the sweep on Wednesday afternoon against the Minnesota Twins.
They’re coming off an 8-1 victory over the Twins on Tuesday night in a game in which infielder Anthony Volpe recorded two hits to continue his strong stretch since being recalled on Sept. 10.
However, ahead of Wednesday’s game, Yankees manager Aaron Boone decided to make a notable lineup move involving Volpe.
Yankees Announce Volpe Move
After spending his last few games batting in the seven-hole and clearly adapting just fine at the plate, Boone has decided to move Volpe back down to the nine spot for the series finale.
Other notable lineup changes include superstar Aaron Judge rejoining the lineup after a night off, catcher Austin Wells replacing Ali Sanchez behind the plate, and Jose Caballero getting the day off.
Here’s the full Yankees lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Yankees 9/16 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF A. Judge RF L. García Jr. 1B S. Jones CF G. Lombard Jr. SS R. McMahon 3B A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B C. Rodón SP.”
Yankees 9/16
B. Rice DH
C. Bellinger LF
A. Judge RF
L. García Jr. 1B
S. Jones CF
G. Lombard Jr. SS
R. McMahon 3B
A. Wells C
A. Volpe 2B
C. Rodón SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 16, 2026
Volpe’s 2026 Season
It’s been a challenging 2026 season for Volpe, who’s in his fourth year with the Yankees.
He began the season on the IL, and for the bulk of his campaign in the majors, he just hasn’t been able to find much of a rhythm.
Entering Wednesday, Volpe has found success since the Yankees sent him to Triple-A on Aug. 4 and recalled him last week, but he still owns a .249 average across 62 games and 189 at-bats. He has recorded 23 runs, 47 hits, two home runs, and 24 RBIs while slugging .344 with a .676 OPS.
Despite this, he has an opportunity down the stretch of the regular season to prove why he belongs on the postseason roster and become an everyday-type player.

item.content:encoded:
The most iconic Mickey Mantle image fetched an insane price.
Ron Firman of Rye, N.Y., purchased for $3 million the first edition of the non-autographed, PSA-authenticated photo of the iconic Yankees center fielder that later became Mantle’s legendary 1952 Topps card.
The picture of Mantle was sold at a private sale brokered by Hunt Auctions.
It is a PSA Type 1 photo, meaning it is a “first-generation photograph, developed from the original negative, during the period (within approximately two years of when the picture was taken),” according to psacard.com.
That picture was taken by an unknown International News Service photographer at Yankees spring training in Phoenix on March 5, 1951, though the photographer carried no credit so it’s unclear if the individual was a company staffer or a freelancer.
“The demand for high-end original Type I photographs from new collectors and investors coming into the space is at an all-time high,” said PSA photo authenticator Henry Yee.
“The supply, however, for this material is extremely scarce. When an item of this caliber is offered for sale, often it is sold privately and does not even make it to public auction — such as in this case.”
Highly graded copies of Mantle’s iconic 1952 Topps card have fetched obscene prices at auction, including a record $12.6 million in August 2022.
That 1952 card is not his rookie card, though.
Mantle’s rookie card is from Bowman’s 1951 set, which has sold for as much as $843,750, though that card is not a real picture but a painted image.
The 1952 Topps card is a real image on cardboard and one of the most famous images in all of sports memorabilia.
In PSA’s pool, there are only 2,075 copies of Mantle’s 1952 Topps card across all grades.
Mantle played for the Yankees from 1951-66 and authored one of baseball’s most legendary careers, primarily manning center field as a left-handed-swinging power hitter from Oklahoma.
He tallied 536 homers, but his body began to fall apart after the 1961 home run chase with Roger Maris, when Mantle hit 54 home runs and drove in 128 runs, while Maris hit a then-record 61 homers and drove in 141.

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] Gerrit Cole Ya No Es Una Elección Segura Ahora Que Los Yankees Se Están Replanteando Su Plan De Pitcheo Para La Postemporada
item.dc:creator: Sara Molnick

item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK — Durante casi toda la última década, a Gerrit Cole le tocaban automáticamente los partidos más importantes de los Yankees.
Esa seguridad se ha esfumado.
A menos de dos semanas de que termine octubre, el lanzador que marcaba la diferencia en el equipo se ha convertido en su mayor incógnita. La velocidad sigue ahí, pero los resultados se han deteriorado en el peor momento posible. Aaron Boone ha intentado restarle importancia a la preocupación. Pero lo que pasa sigue haciendo que eso sea cada vez más difícil.
Cole, ganador del Premio Cy Young de los Yankees en 2023, ha encajado siete jonrones en sus dos últimas salidas, la cifra más alta en cualquier racha de dos salidas de su carrera, según MLB.com. El que antes era una apuesta segura para el primer partido ha bajado puestos en la jerarquía de octubre y ha generado un auténtico debate sobre si debería ser el lanzador titular en un partido a vida o muerte.
Para un equipo de los Yankees que tiene el mejor promedio de carreras limpias permitidas (ERA) del béisbol, esto es como una grieta en los cimientos. Nueva York se aseguró el lunes su plaza en los playoffs y ahora tiene un balance de 88-63. El pitcheo es la razón por la que el club cree que puede llegar lejos. Se suponía que Cole iba a ser el pilar de esa fortaleza, no que se convirtiera en su mayor incertidumbre.
Un problema mental que aterroriza a los Yankees
El 6 de septiembre, Cole encajó jonrones de los tres primeros bateadores de los Padres a los que se enfrentó. Fernando Tatis Jr., Jake Cronenworth y Manny Machado conectaron tres jonrones seguidos.
Seis días después, los Mets le dieron una paliza al as de los Yankees en una goleada por 12-2. Francisco Lindor conectó un jonrón con el tercer lanzamiento de Cole. Más tarde, el novato Carson Benge también le mandó la pelota fuera del campo con un slider. Cole aguantó 4 1/3 entradas, encajó cinco carreras y tres jonrones, y se llevó abucheos al salir del campo.
Tras el partido, su explicación hizo que la derrota de los Yankees pareciera aún peor.
Cole tiene una efectividad de 6,08 en sus últimas cuatro salidas, con 17 ponches en 22 2/3 entradas, y ha encajado al menos tres carreras limpias en cuatro partidos seguidos.
En lo que va de temporada, tiene un balance de 8-9, con una efectividad de 3,67 y 20 jonrones permitidos en 115 1/3 entradas. Los Yankees solo han promediado 3,67 carreras en sus salidas, lo que ha convertido partidos que antes parecían pan comido en auténticas loterías.
Lo que realmente preocupa a los Yankees
La preocupación no es que Cole haya perdido de repente su nivel de Grandes Ligas. Es por qué los bateadores se ven tan cómodos frente a él.
Los analistas de YES Network, David Cone y Paul O’Neill, plantearon la posibilidad de que Cole esté delatando sus lanzamientos, lo que podría explicar por qué los bateadores han sabido manejar una bola rápida que sigue alcanzando las 98 mph.
El entrenador de lanzadores, Matt Blake, no lo descartó.
«Es posible», dijo Blake, y añadió que «esa es una de las cosas que vamos a analizar».
Blake también señaló un problema más sencillo. Cole está lanzando strikes a un ritmo sin precedentes en su carrera, pero demasiados se quedan en el centro del strike zone.
«Tenemos que sacar la bola de la parte más ancha del plato», dijo Blake. «Además, quizá tengamos que mejorar la ejecución con dos strikes para lanzar a mejores zonas».
Cole ha reconocido el problema sin pretender haberlo resuelto.
«Hay que empezar a hacer ajustes», dijo Cole.
También rechazó la teoría de que delata sus lanzamientos, diciendo que sus lanzamientos deberían seguir dándonos margen incluso si los bateadores los anticipan.
«Aunque sepan (lo que viene), sigue siendo difícil de batear», dijo Cole. «Mis lanzamientos deberían darnos más margen de error».
Cómo está cambiando la rotación
La mala racha de Cole ha trastocado la jerarquía de la rotación.
Cam Schlittler, en una segunda temporada espectacular, se ha revelado como el mejor lanzador del equipo y un probable candidato al premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana. Se perfila como el abridor del primer partido. Max Fried, que vuelve tras una lesión en el codo, y Carlos Rodón tienen ambos un promedio de carreras limpias por debajo de 3,00 y parecen opciones más seguras para los primeros partidos de la serie.
El enfrentamiento complica aún más las cosas. Es probable que los Yankees se enfrenten a Boston en una serie de comodín al mejor de tres. Cole tiene una efectividad de 5,30 en su carrera contra los Red Sox, y solo los Mets le han bateado con más fuerza.
El veterano columnista Joel Sherman resumió la cuestión de octubre en una sola palabra: «correa». Según su hipótesis, Cole empezaría un partido de mitad de temporada con mucho menos margen de error.
«Creo que Schlittler, Fried y Cole van a ser los titulares», dijo Sherman. «La diferencia es que a Cole le van a dar muy, muy poco margen, algo que, por lo general, no habría tenido».
Sherman también vinculó directamente el techo de los Yankees en la postemporada a que Cole y Aaron Judge recuperen su mejor forma.
«Los Yankees podrían quedarse fuera de los playoffs en menos de 48 horas o podrían ganar la Serie Mundial», dijo Sherman. «Ambas opciones están sobre la mesa y las posibilidades de éxito aumentan mucho más si Cole y Judge se ponen las pilas en las próximas dos semanas, porque son Gerrit Cole y Aaron Judge, y son grandes jugadores cuando están en forma».
Los datos sobre los lanzamientos con efecto explican el colapso
Cole ha mantenido a los bateadores zurdos en un OPS de 0,683. El problema son los bateadores diestros, que tienen un slugging de 0,448 contra él, la cifra más alta que han registrado los diestros en cualquier temporada de su carrera.
Las bolas con efecto del as de los Yankees son las que están causando más daño. Los bateadores diestros tienen un promedio de slugging de 0,652 contra su curva, con diferencia la peor cifra de su carrera. Tienen un promedio de slugging de 0,463 contra su slider, también un récord personal y, con holgada diferencia, su peor marca como jugador de los Yankees.
Además, esos lanzamientos están fallando menos. Su curva solo ha generado un 17 % de fallos contra los bateadores diestros, mientras que su slider se sitúa en el 25 %. Además, está lanzando el slider en el centro de la zona contra los bateadores diestros con la mayor frecuencia de su carrera, lo que explica tanto la reducción de los fallos como los contactos más fuertes.
Los modelos de calidad de los lanzamientos muestran el mismo deterioro. El slider de Cole ha bajado de una puntuación de 125 en Stuff+ en 2020 a 106 esta temporada. La curva de la estrella de los Yankees ha bajado de 120 a 104. Ambas siguen estando por encima de la media, pero el margen que antes le hacía imparable se ha reducido.
Cole cumplió 36 años el 8 de septiembre y está en su primera temporada tras recuperarse de una operación de Tommy John, un año que, según la medicina deportiva, suele ser menos brillante que el segundo. Ya sea por un problema mecánico, por delatar sus lanzamientos o por simple cansancio, Nueva York tiene menos de dos semanas para encontrar la respuesta.
Por ahora, el as que en su día se encargaba de las tareas más importantes está haciendo una prueba para un papel en octubre que antes dominaba.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario más abajo.

item.title: [Pinstripes Nation] Seis Bajas En Los Yankees En 15 Días: ¿qué Hay Detrás De Los Cambios Radicales De Cashman En El Departamento De Ojeadores Internacionales?

item.content:encoded:
BRONX, N.Y. — Los Yankees ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada y siguen a 3 1/2 partidos del Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana. Pero una de las decisiones más importantes que ha tomado la organización este mes de septiembre no tiene nada que ver con la alineación de Aaron Boone ni con los planes de pitcheo para octubre.
Esto ha dado lugar a seis despidos en lo que va de septiembre.
Todo esto está pasando a miles de millas del Yankee Stadium, en la República Dominicana, Venezuela y otros mercados donde se descubre a los futuros Yankees años antes de que la mayoría de los aficionados sepan siquiera sus nombres.
De esa cantera salieron Robinson Canó, Alfonso Soriano, Gary Sánchez e Iván Nova. Los Yankees siguieron invirtiendo ahí a medida que cambiaban las normas sobre bonificaciones, la tecnología y los métodos de evaluación de jugadores amateurs.
La presión sobre esa área lleva meses aumentando. Donny Rowland, director de ojeadores internacionales desde hacía mucho tiempo, no renovó su contrato cuando este expiró en noviembre. Los Yankees ascendieron entonces a Mario Garza, que llevaba 16 años en la organización y tenía experiencia en el desarrollo de jugadores, las operaciones en Latinoamérica y el desarrollo del béisbol, para que se encargara de los ojeadores internacionales en enero.
La transición tuvo un coste inmediato. Wandy Asigen, uno de los mejores jugadores de la promoción internacional de 2026, se echó atrás en el acuerdo que tenía previsto con los Yankees tras la marcha de Rowland y fichó por los Mets por 3,9 millones de dólares. Nueva York también empezó el periodo de fichajes con un fondo de 5,44 millones de dólares, el más bajo de la MLB (empatado con otro equipo) tras perder un millón de dólares por fichar a Max Fried.
Cuando Garza se hizo cargo, Brian Cashman describió algo que iba más allá de un simple cambio de personal.
«Es un gran evaluador de talento», dijo Cashman. «Conoce nuestros sistemas. Ya sabe todo el personal que queremos tener. Quieres evaluación, quieres que todo esté conectado con la ciencia del rendimiento y el análisis de datos. Eso le dará ventaja a la hora de relanzar ese departamento y seguir adelante».
Esas declaraciones públicas cobran ahora importancia porque dejaron claro, meses antes de septiembre, que Nueva York veía el departamento como algo que había que reconstruir, en lugar de simplemente mantener.
El relanzamiento se ha convertido en una reestructuración más amplia de los Yankees
Ese relanzamiento se ha acelerado.
Cinco empleados del departamento de ojeadores internacionales de los Yankees no han sido renovados en lo que el periodista Francys Romero ha descrito como una «primera oleada». Se trata de los ojeadores de la zona de la República Dominicana José Sabino y Arturo Peña Jr., el ojeador de la zona de Santo Domingo Moisés Brito, el asistente de vídeo Miguel Mojica y el supervisor de Venezuela José Gavidia.
Romero describió los cambios como parte de un plan más amplio.
«Los Yankees tienen previsto reestructurar su departamento de ojeadores internacionales y, según fuentes del sector, ya han despedido a cinco personas en los últimos días. Entre los ojeadores que no seguirán están José Sabino y Arturo Peña Jr. (ojeador de la zona de Cibao, República Dominicana), Moisés Brito (ojeador de la zona de Santo Domingo), Miguel Mojica (asistente de vídeo) y José Gavidia (supervisor de Venezuela)».
Estas medidas se produjeron tras la salida del veterano ojeador Víctor Mata, cuya trayectoria en los Yankees se prolongó durante más de tres décadas. Mata ayudó a evaluar o fichar a Canó, Sánchez, Soriano, Nova y Zoilo Almonte.
La naturaleza exacta de la salida de Mata sigue siendo objeto de debate. Romero informó de que los Yankees lo dejaron marchar. El periodista Mike Rodríguez ofreció una versión diferente, afirmando que Mata se retiró y recibió las prestaciones asociadas a su larga trayectoria en el equipo. Los Yankees no han dado públicamente una explicación detallada.
La cronología apunta a un reinicio planificado
La racha es más larga que los movimientos de esta semana.
A Rowland no le renovaron el contrato en noviembre. Garza fue nombrado en enero y Cashman utilizó públicamente la palabra «relanzamiento». Los Yankees funcionaron entonces toda la temporada bajo un nuevo liderazgo antes de la marcha de Mata y los cinco cambios adicionales en la plantilla que se produjeron en septiembre.
Esto apunta más bien a un reajuste estructural que a una reacción ante un solo prospecto o una sola promoción de fichajes.
Había motivos para replantearse los resultados. Un análisis de FanGraphs sobre el sistema de cantera de los Yankees, publicado en marzo, señalaba que el club solía destinar una gran parte de su fondo de bonificaciones internacionales a uno o dos jugadores caros y que demasiadas de esas apuestas millonarias no habían dado los frutos esperados.
En ese mismo informe se decía que el sistema necesitaba más talento entre los jugadores de campo tras las últimas salidas por graduación. Eso no aclara por qué se despidió a ningún ojeador, pero ayuda a entender por qué los Yankees se replantearían cómo identifican, valoran y forman a los jugadores internacionales.
La marcha de Asigen hizo que el tema cobrara más relevancia. Este campocorto de 16 años estaba considerado uno de los mejores jugadores de su generación y se esperaba que firmara con los Yankees, pero cambió de planes tras la salida de Rowland.
Ahora los comentarios que hizo Cashman en enero parecen más importantes
La pista más clara sobre qué hay detrás de la reorganización de los Yankees podría haber llegado ocho meses antes de los últimos cambios.
La descripción que hizo Cashman de Garza hacía hincapié en la colaboración entre la evaluación, la ciencia del rendimiento y el análisis de datos. El currículum de Garza une todas esas áreas. Antes de este puesto, fue director de desarrollo de béisbol en 2024 y 2025, y anteriormente trabajó en operaciones en Latinoamérica y en el desarrollo de jugadores internacionales.
Esto hace que los cambios parezcan menos un rechazo al ojeo tradicional y más un intento de cambiar cómo circula la información de ojeo por la organización.
El ojeo internacional sigue dependiendo de las relaciones, la evaluación presencial y el conocimiento local. La carrera de Mata puso de manifiesto ese valor. Pero ahora los Yankees están colocando al frente del departamento a un líder con experiencia reciente en desarrollo y sistemas.
La apuesta es importante. Nueva York está dejando atrás a miembros del equipo con profundas raíces en Latinoamérica, al tiempo que pide a un nuevo grupo que mantenga esas relaciones y modernice la evaluación al mismo tiempo.
El veredicto tardará años en salir
No hay resultados inmediatos que reflejen una reforma en el sistema de ojeadores internacionales.
Un cambio en la alineación se puede valorar esa misma noche. Pero una decisión que afecte a un joven promesa de 16 años puede que no dé frutos en las Grandes Ligas hasta dentro de cinco o seis años.
Eso es lo que hace que el momento sea tan significativo. Los Yankees tienen un balance de 88-63, se han asegurado un puesto en octubre y ocupan la primera plaza de comodín de la Liga Americana. Sin embargo, estos cambios están pensados para las plantillas mucho más allá de la actual carrera por los playoffs.
La cronología que se conoce está clara: Rowland se va, ascienden a Garza, se pierde a uno de los mejores fichajes, Mata se marcha y no se renueva a otros cinco miembros del personal internacional. Lo que los Yankees no han dicho públicamente es si habrá más cambios.
Por ahora, las declaraciones de Cashman en enero son las que ofrecen una explicación más clara. Los Yankees querían relanzar el departamento y vincular más estrechamente el trabajo de ojeadores con la ciencia del rendimiento y el análisis de datos.
Ocho meses después, ese relanzamiento está cambiando el perfil de las personas que decidirán qué jóvenes jugadores entrarán próximamente en el sistema de los Yankees.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario más abajo.

item.title: [roundtable.io] Cody Bellinger's Resurgence Means Everything to the Yankees
item.dc:creator: Matthew Schmidt
item.description: The resurgence of Cody Bellinger has been key in the New York Yankees' recent push. For a while there, New York Yankees outfielder Cody Bellinger was completely dormant offensively. item.content:encoded:
The resurgence of Cody Bellinger has been key in the New York Yankees' recent push.
For a while there, New York Yankees outfielder Cody Bellinger was completely dormant offensively. Between July and August, Bellinger managed just one home run and 10 RBI, and while he missed time with a hamstring injury, he wasn't effective even when he was healthy.
Bellinger posted a sub-.700 OPS for three straight months heading into September, and it was beginning to look like one of those years for the former NL MVP. This even though he got off to a torrid start this season.
But since the calendar flipped to September, Bellinger looks like a different hitter.
The lefty slugger is slashing .370/.375/.648 with four homers and 12 RBI over 56 plate appearances through the first half of the month, most recently going 3-for-4 with a two-run blast against the Minnesota Twins on Tuesday night.
Has Bellinger's resurgence coincided with the return of Aaron Judge? Somewhat. Judge came back on Sept. 8, and since then, Bellinger has mashed four long balls and has a hit in all but one game.
However, Bellinger was also rolling the first week of September, and Judge was not in the lineup when Bellinger smacked his two-run homer Tuesday evening.
There is no question that Bellinger's dip in production was largely a result of both Judge and Giancarlo Stanton being sidelined. The 31-year-old is no longer the player he was from his early Los Angeles Dodgers days when he could carry a lineup. He need support.
But when he gets it, he becomes incredibly valuable.
Bellinger is slashing .272/.347/.443 with 16 home runs and 71 RBI over 527 plate appearances on the campaign. Has he been quite as good as last year when he smashed 29 dingers while posting an .813 OPS? No, and we cannot ignore just how invisible he was for such a long stretch when the Yankees desperately needed him to produce.
But the $162.5 million man is getting hot at the right time, with the MLB playoffs starting in less than two weeks. And we know just how outstanding he is in he field, as Bellinger has posted an incredible 19 defensive runs saved and six outs above average in 2026.
Hopefully, Bellinger can sustain his recent surge heading into the postseason, especially considering it appears that Stanton will remain on the shelf.
The Yankees paid Bellinger like an All-Star. That requires hitting like one. We'll see if it can continue.
